title: Time, Attendance & Reliability
summary: Learn why attendance, punctuality, preparation, and reliable communication matter in the workplace and how your time commitments can affect other people.
objectives: Explain how attendance and punctuality affect coworkers, customers, schedules, and operations.
Distinguish being present from being ready to begin work.
Identify responsible communication when you may be late or absent.

vocab.def: Being present when you are expected to work, participate, or report for an assigned responsibility.
Arriving or being ready at the expected time.
A pattern of consistently meeting reasonable commitments and communicating when circumstances change.
Having the information, materials, equipment, and readiness needed to begin work appropriately.

sections.heading: Your time affects other people
sections.body: Workplaces operate through connected schedules and responsibilities. When one person is unexpectedly late or absent, coworkers, customers, meetings, handoffs, transportation, production, or services may also be affected.

sections.heading: Being present is not always the same as being ready
sections.body: A worker may arrive at the correct time but still be unprepared to begin. Professional readiness can include having required materials, information, access, equipment, clothing, or other role-specific requirements ready.

sections.heading: Reliability is a pattern
sections.body: One difficult day does not define a person's reliability. Workplaces usually develop trust through patterns of attendance, punctuality, preparation, follow-through, and communication.

sections.heading: Communicate problems early
sections.body: If you know you may be late or unable to attend, use the workplace's required process as early as reasonably possible. Do not wait until other people discover the problem themselves.

practice.prompt: Your shift begins at 9:00, but at 8:15 you realize transportation problems may make you late. What is the strongest response?
practice.answer: Use the workplace's required communication process as early as possible, provide an accurate status, and follow any instructions about coverage or next steps.

practice.prompt: You arrive exactly on time but still need ten minutes to gather everything required to begin your assigned work. Were you fully prepared to start at the expected time?
practice.answer: Not necessarily. Punctuality may include being ready to begin when work is scheduled to start.

quiz.question: Which behavior best demonstrates workplace reliability?
options: Consistently meeting commitments and communicating early when circumstances change
Arriving whenever convenient as long as the work eventually gets done
Waiting until after a missed shift to explain what happened
Assuming coworkers will automatically cover unexpected absences
quiz.answer: Consistently meeting commitments and communicating early when circumstances change

lab.objective: Review several simulated attendance and punctuality situations and identify the operational impact, the worker's responsibility, and the most appropriate communication response.

reflectionPrompt: How can one person's attendance or punctuality affect people who are not their supervisor?
